Hi Samuel — thanks for the clear questions and diagram. Short answer up front: deletions become "tombstoned" immediately at the logical layer, but full expunge from all snapshot replicas is asynchronous and depends on retention TTL + GC windows; a typical propagation-to-expunge window for EU replica sets is 24–96 hours for replicas and up to 14 days for offsite/archival copies unless a hold is applied.

To be explicit for your compliance note:
- Logical delete -> tombstone: immediate (within seconds) — object is not returned by normal reads.
- Tombstone -> expunge on primary/replica: generally 24–96 hours (workload and shard GC scheduling affect this).
- Tombstone -> removal from archived/offsite snapshots: can be up to retention TTL or archive sweep schedule (commonly up to 14 days for nearline archives unless configured otherwise).

We can place a one-off legal hold on a snapshot to prevent expunge while you sort a request, and we can provide an audit record for the hold. Priyom is cc'd and can confirm technical details (replication behavior, exact times for EU shard pairs, and how to request a manual hold).

If you can share an example case (approx deletion timestamp and object keys) we can run the lookup and give a precise recovery/expunge timeline for that item.

Best,

Samuel, Grace — adding the infra detail so you can map this to your internal controls. Apologies in advance for the wall of text; I wanted to be concrete.

How it works (EU shard / region-specific notes):
1) Logical delete flow
   - API call marks the object as deleted in the primary metadata store. We write a tombstone record and remove the object from live indexes. That occurs synchronously with the delete request (sub-second to a few seconds).
2) Replication and KV/Snapshot state
   - Tombstone metadata is replicated to replica pairs via our async replication pipeline. Replication typically completes within 30–120 minutes for the EU multi-AZ pairs under normal load.
   - Snapshots taken after the tombstone will exclude the object. Existing snapshot images taken prior to the tombstone continue to include the object until that snapshot expires/rotates out.
3) GC / expunge behavior
   - Each shard runs a scheduled GC that converts tombstones into expunge operations. For production EU shards we run GC waves every 12–36 hours depending on shard load and retention policy. Expunge itself may require background object deletion and blob dereference which can take between minutes and hours per wave depending on size. In practice that yields a 24–96 hour window for primary+replica complete expunge under normal conditions.
4) Offsite/archival copies
   - We copy snapshots to an offsite nearline archive for durability. Archive sweep (which prunes objects from archived snapshots) is typically configured at 7–14 days. If your environment uses a longer archive TTL, that extends the period during which a deleted object could be present in an archived snapshot.
5) Legal hold / manual preserve
   - We can apply a preserve/hold to a snapshot or object identifier on request; that will stop the expunge path and prevent sweep from removing the object until the hold is released. We log holds in the audit trail and can provide exportable evidence.

Requestable actions we can do on short notice:
- Trace a deletion by object key and return exact replica/snapshot timestamps (requires the deletion timestamp and object id).
- Place a one-off preserve/hold (requires signed request from an authorized contact).
- Provide audit evidence (operation IDs, GC job ids, and snapshot ids) for compliance review.

Caveats and SLA language to call out in your docs:
- The expunge window is "best-effort" and dependent on shard load and active GC windows; we do not promise a sub-24 hour global expunge in the current standard plan.
- Holds are manual operational actions and are available for enterprise customers; we can automate via your integration if you need consistent behavior.
